title: The electron transport chain
canonical_question: How does the electron transport chain move electrons and build a gradient?
summary: Membrane complexes pass electrons and pump protons.
Oxygen is the final electron acceptor.

sections.heading: A chain of hand-offs
sections.body_md: The electron transport chain is a series of protein complexes set in the inner membrane of the mitochondrion. High-energy electrons enter at one end and are passed from one complex to the next. Each hand-off releases a little energy.

sections.heading: Pumping protons
sections.body_md: The energy released at each step is used to push protons from one side of the inner membrane to the other. This builds up a difference in proton concentration, a kind of stored pressure, across the membrane.

sections.heading: Oxygen at the finish
sections.body_md: At the last complex the electrons are handed to oxygen, which combines with protons to form water. Without oxygen to accept the electrons, the whole chain backs up and stops.

key_points: Each hand-off pumps protons to build a gradient.
Oxygen accepts the electrons at the end and forms water.
